question: What is the main reason to use presentation software in midwifery studies?

options.A: To calculate student attendance and examination scores
options.B: To store patient records securely in a database
options.C: To combine text, images, and layouts for better learning
options.D: To replace clinical textbooks completely with digital files

explanation: Presentation software brings together visual and text elements to make educational content easier to understand. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do slides with simple text and clear pictures work well when teaching community groups?

options.A: They maintain audience engagement during health talks
options.B: They guarantee that everyone in the audience can read English
options.C: They reduce the amount of electricity needed by the projector
options.D: They eliminate the need for the speaker to explain anything

explanation: Visuals paired with simple text prevent the audience from getting overwhelmed and keep attention focused on the core health message. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h1)

question: Where are the command tabs and tool groups found in PowerPoint?
explanation: The ribbon sits at the top of the window and holds all the primary editing tabs and tools. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which part of the PowerPoint screen is meant for typing speaker reminders and talking points?
explanation: The notes pane at the bottom provides a space for lecturers to type reminders that the audience cannot see on the main slide. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why are sans-serif fonts preferred for slides shown in large lecture halls?

options.A: They are the only font style recognized by modern projectors
options.B: They project clearly and are easy to read from a distance
options.C: They automatically correct spelling errors made by the lecturer
options.D: They take up less memory space on the computer hard drive

explanation: Clean letterforms without decorative edges prevent blurring and keep text readable for students sitting at the back of the room. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which of these practices should be avoided when designing teaching slides?

options.A: Overcrowding slides with long paragraphs of text
options.B: Using high-contrast color combinations for text
options.C: Applying bullet points to summarize main teaching ideas
options.D: Leaving blank space around images and headers

explanation: Putting too much text on a slide overwhelms listeners and makes the presentation hard to follow. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which tab on the PowerPoint ribbon is used to add pictures and video clips to a slide?
explanation: The Insert tab contains commands for adding external media such as pictures, shapes, audio, and video files. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h4)

question: A midwife wants to show a video clip of a delivery process during a lecture. What is the best practice for using this media?

options.A: Keep the clip short and ensure file compatibility beforehand
options.B: Embed a very large video file so it takes up the whole slide
options.C: Play the entire documentary without pausing or stopping it
options.D: Rely on an active internet connection to stream a long video

explanation: Short, pre-tested clips prevent technical delays and keep students focused on the specific teaching point. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h4)

question: How do sudden, flashy slide animations affect students during a clinical lecture?

options.A: They replace the need for clear learning objectives
options.B: They distract learners from the core medical content
options.C: They improve the retention of complex midwifery procedures
options.D: They help students take faster notes in their workbooks

explanation: Excessive or flashy visual effects draw attention away from the actual educational message being taught. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h5)

question: What type of slide is recommended at the very start of a health education presentation?

options.A: A slide stating the learning objectives
options.B: A slide containing a complex statistical data table
options.C: A slide with a long list of vocabulary definitions
options.D: A slide filled with detailed reference citations

explanation: Starting with clear objectives helps set expectations and guides student focus for the rest of the lecture. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h5)

question: A midwife is preparing slides on malaria prevention for a rural community center with unreliable power. What is the best precaution?

options.A: Increase the brightness setting on the projector to maximum
options.B: Ensure the laptop is fully charged and carry backup printouts
options.C: Rely entirely on online cloud storage to access the slides
options.D: Cancel the lecture until a permanent generator is installed

explanation: Having a charged device and physical backups protects the teaching session against sudden power cuts or equipment failure. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is reading every word directly from the projection screen discouraged during a health talk?

options.A: Audience members read faster than the speaker talks, causing boredom
options.B: Projector bulbs burn out faster if text remains static for too long
options.C: PowerPoint software automatically penalizes speakers who read text
options.D: It is against the official copyright laws for medical presentations

explanation: Reading word-for-word makes the presentation monotonous and disconnects the speaker from the audience. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T3#BMP123_U3_T3_h6)
